_comment: Synthetic-safe safety-gaps register (CHI-323 3d). Illustrative accepted-gap entries for the Safety surface — never real confidential posture. Each actionable gap names a real gate surface id in closingEdit.surface so the 'work on this' launcher can open the right control. Edit to reflect a real operator's accepted gaps on a private instance.
header: Known, accepted gaps in the local egress posture. Each is a deliberate trade-off with a blast radius and a revisit trigger, not an oversight.

gaps.title: No per-transaction spend cap configured
gaps.exposure: A runaway agent loop could spend without an automatic ceiling; only the confirm step stands in the way.
gaps.acceptedWhy: Early single-operator use; every paid action is still confirm-first, so the practical blast radius is one confirmed call at a time.
gaps.blastRadius: One confirmed transaction; no unattended spend path exists yet.

gaps.title: New tools default to the strictest bucket until classified
gaps.exposure: An unclassified tool is treated as deny-by-default, which is safe but can block a legitimate new integration until its class is set.
gaps.acceptedWhy: Fail-closed is the right default; the cost is a one-time classify step per new tool.
gaps.blastRadius: A blocked tool call, never an unintended send.

gaps.title: Tier-2 confirms depend on a single second channel
gaps.exposure: If the second channel is down, Tier-2 edits cannot be confirmed until it is restored.
gaps.acceptedWhy: A failed second-channel send is loud and blocks the edit rather than silently proceeding, so the failure mode is availability, not safety.
gaps.blastRadius: A temporarily un-confirmable Tier-2 edit; no write happens without the code.
gaps.revisitTrigger: Add a fallback channel if Tier-2 edits become frequent.
